articles.title: Club News and Announcements
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) outlines its June and July activities, featuring numerous star parties, ATM workshops, astronomy classes, and general meetings with guest speakers. The article also details a significant potential donation of land near Hollister to serve as a dedicated dark sky observing site, emphasizing its excellent sky quality and protected location. Additionally, SJAA issues an urgent call for volunteers to take over newsletter circulation duties, as the current team is stepping down.

articles.title: Coyote Lake County Park Summer Star Party Series
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) and The Astronomy Connection (TAC) are hosting the first of a series of public star parties at Coyote Lake County Park on Saturday, June 3rd, from 9:00 to 12:00 p.m. This event offers a convenient observing site, free for astronomical use, and will take place at the Boat Launch Ramp Parking Lot, about 2 miles from the Ranger Station, to accommodate a larger turnout based on last year's success.

articles.title: Broken Comets and Drifting Dunes
articles.summary: This article provides an observing guide for June 2006, highlighting optimal viewing conditions for Jupiter, Neptune, Uranus, and Pluto, along with advice on observing the fragmented Comet 73P/Schwassmann-Wachmann 3. It also details close conjunctions of Saturn, Mars, and the Beehive cluster, and discusses recent Cassini data revealing extensive dune fields on Titan, challenging previous assumptions of methane seas.

articles.title: Eclipse over Egypt
articles.summary: The article recounts an expedition to El-Sallum Matrouh, Egypt, for the total solar eclipse on March 29, 2006, detailing travel challenges, equipment setup, and the awe-inspiring observation of the corona and other phenomena despite technical difficulties with optical alignment. It also presents a separate analysis of the Tully-Fisher Relation, a method for determining galactic distances based on rotational speed and intrinsic brightness, examining its effectiveness across different galaxy types and spectral bands using the LEDA database.

articles.title: NASA Space Place
articles.summary: NASA's New Millennium Program (NMP), run by JPL, tests advanced, unproven technologies in space to validate their readiness for future missions, thereby reducing risk. The program takes lab-proven innovations, such as Autonomous Navigation (AutoNav) and solar sails, and subjects them to the extreme space environment to enable the development of smaller, lighter, and more capable spacecraft. NMP plays a crucial role in making future, previously impossible, space exploration and scientific missions viable.

articles.title: Dr. Peter Jenniskens on Meteor Showers and their Parent Comets
articles.summary: Dr. Peter Jenniskens of The SETI Institute will deliver a talk at Houge Park on June 10, discussing meteor showers and their parent comets. He will explore how meteoroid streams form, recent findings from space missions, the risk of meteor impacts, and how meteors might have contributed to life on Earth. The presentation will also cover historical meteor observing campaigns, including those involving SJAA members, and insights from his new book "Meteor showers and their parent comets."

articles.title: SJAA loaner scope status
articles.summary: This article outlines the status of the San Jose Astronomical Association's (SJAA) telescope loaner program for its members. It provides a comprehensive list of telescopes currently available for immediate loan, along with details on scopes that are presently borrowed or have extended loan periods. SJAA members can contact Mike Koop to arrange borrowing a scope, with pickups typically at SJAA events.
